是時循舊，王公重臣皆呼其名，高祖常謂沖為中書而不名之。 文明太后崩後，高祖居喪，引見待接有加。 及議禮儀律令，潤飾辭旨，刊定輕重，高祖雖自下筆，無不訪決焉。 沖竭忠奉上，知無不盡，出入憂勤，形於顏色，雖舊臣戚輔，莫能逮之，無不服其明斷慎密而歸心焉。 於是天下翕然，及殊方聽望，咸宗奇之。 高祖亦深相杖信，親敬彌甚，君臣之間，情義莫二。 及改置百司，開建五等，以沖參定典式，封滎陽郡開國侯，食邑八百戶，拜廷尉卿。 尋遷侍中、吏部尚書、咸陽王師。 東宮既建，拜太子少傅。 高祖初依周禮，置夫、嬪之列，以沖女為夫人。
At that time, following custom, princes, dukes, and high ministers were all addressed by their personal names. The Emperor always called Chong "Director of the Palace Secretariat" rather than use his name. After Empress Dowager Wenming died, the Emperor observed mourning. In audiences his treatment of Chong was especially generous. When ritual, law, and statutes were debated, he polished the wording and fixed penalties and mitigations. Though the Emperor drafted the texts himself, he always consulted Chong before deciding. Chong served the throne with complete loyalty, withholding nothing he knew. His constant care and exertion showed in his face. Even old ministers and kinsmen among the chief counselors could not match him. All admired his clarity of judgment and careful discretion, and gave him their hearts. Thereupon the realm fell into harmony, and even those in distant regions who heard of him and looked his way regarded him with admiration. The Emperor also relied on and trusted him deeply, treating him with ever greater personal regard. Between ruler and minister their bond of loyalty and affection was singular. When the hundred offices were reorganized and the five ranks of nobility established, Chong was appointed to help set the canonical forms. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang Commandery with a fief of eight hundred households and appointed Director of the Court of Justice. Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Preceptor to the Prince of Xianyang. Once the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. When the Emperor first followed the Rites of Zhou in establishing the ranks of lady and consort, he made Chong's daughter a Lady.
37
詔曰：「昔軒皇誕御，垂棟宇之構； 爰歷三代，興宮觀之式。 然茅茨土堦，昭德於上代； 層臺廣厦，崇威於中葉。 良由文質異宜，華樸殊禮故也。 是以周成繼業，營明堂於東都； 漢祖聿興，建未央於咸鎬。 蓋所以尊嚴皇威，崇重帝德，豈好奢惡儉，苟弊民力者哉？ 我皇運統天，協纂乾曆，銳意四方，未遑建制，宮室之度，頗為未允。 太祖初基，雖粗有經式，自茲厥後，復多營改。 至於三元慶饗，萬國充庭，觀光之使，具瞻有闕。 朕以寡德，猥承洪緒，運屬休期，事鍾昌運，宜遵遠度，式茲宮宇。 指訓規模，事昭於平日； 明堂、太廟，已成於昔年。 又因往歲之豐資，藉民情之安逸，將以今春營改正殿。 違犯時令，行之惕然。 但朔土多寒，事殊南夏，自非裁度當春，興役徂暑，則廣制崇基，莫由克就。 成功立事，非委賢莫可； 改制規模，非任能莫濟。 尚書沖器懷淵博，經度明遠，可領將作大匠； 司空、長樂公亮，可與大匠共監興繕。 其去故崇新之宜，修復太極之制，朕當別加指授。」
An edict said: "In antiquity the Yellow Emperor ascended the throne and bequeathed the plan of halls and roofs; through the Three Dynasties the model of palaces and towers was raised. Yet thatched roofs and earthen steps displayed virtue in earlier ages; while tiered terraces and broad halls elevated majesty in the middle age. This was because ornament and substance suited different times, and splendor and simplicity followed different rites. Therefore King Cheng of Zhou, succeeding to the enterprise, built the Bright Hall in the eastern capital; and the Founding Emperor of Han, rising swiftly, raised Weiyang Palace at Xian and Hao. Surely this was to dignify imperial majesty and exalt the Emperor's virtue — not from love of extravagance or hatred of thrift, nor from casually exhausting the people's strength? Our dynasty, its destiny aligned with Heaven, jointly inherited the mandate. Intent on the four quarters, we had no leisure to establish institutions, and the scale of palace halls has fallen somewhat short of what is fitting. When the Grand Ancestor first laid the foundation, there was a rough standard; since then there have been many revisions and rebuildings. When the Three First Days are celebrated and the myriad states fill the court, emissaries come to behold our splendor — yet what meets the eye falls short. I, of slender virtue, have unworthily received the great succession. Our fortune falls in an age of prosperity; affairs coincide with a season of flourishing. We ought to follow distant precedents and thereby give form to these palace halls. Plans and measures have been set forth and made plain in ordinary days; the Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple were completed in years past. Taking also last year's abundant resources and the people's ease of mind, we intend this spring to build and rectify the main hall. To violate the seasons in doing so makes one proceed with trepidation. But the northern lands are largely cold, unlike the south. Unless planning begins in spring and labor proceeds through summer, there is no way to complete so broad a foundation and so lofty a base. To succeed in an enterprise, nothing avails without entrusting it to the worthy; to reform the design, nothing succeeds without assigning the capable. Director of the Secretariat Chong is broad of capacity and profound of mind, clear and far-seeing in planning — let him take charge as Master of Works; the Director of Works, Duke of Changle Liang, may jointly oversee the construction with the Master of Works. As for what is fit in removing the old and elevating the new, and restoring the form of the Grand Ultimate Hall, We shall issue separate instructions."
38
車駕南伐，加沖輔國大將軍，統眾翼從。 自發都至於洛陽，霖雨不霽，仍詔六軍發軫。 高祖戎服執鞭，御馬而出，羣臣啟顙於馬首之前。 高祖曰：「長驅之謀，廟算已定，今大軍將進，公等更欲何云？ 」沖進曰：「臣等不能折衝帷幄，坐制四海，而令南有竊號之渠，實臣等之咎。 陛下以文軌未一，親勞聖駕，臣等誠思亡軀盡命，効死戎行。 然自離都淫雨，士馬困弊，前路尚遙，水潦方甚。 且伊洛境內，小水猶尚致難，況長江浩汗，越在南境。 若營舟檝，必須停滯，師老糧乏，進退為難，矜喪反旆，於義為允。 」高祖曰：「一同之意，前已具論。 卿等正以水雨為難，然天時頗亦可知。 何者？ 夏既炎旱，秋故雨多，玄冬之初，必當開爽。 比後月十間，[12]若雨猶不已，此乃天也，脫於此而晴，行則無害。 古不伐喪，謂諸侯同軌之國，非王者統一之文。 已至於此，何容停駕。 」沖又進曰：「今者之舉，天下所不願，唯陛下欲之。 漢文言，吾獨乘千里馬，竟何至也？ 臣有意而無其辭，敢以死請。 」高祖大怒曰：「方欲經營宇宙，一同區域，而卿等儒生，屢疑大計，斧鉞有常，卿勿復言！ 」策馬將出。 於是大司馬、安定王休，兼左僕射、任城王澄等並殷勤泣諫。 高祖乃諭羣臣曰：「今者興動不小，動而無成，何以示後？ 苟欲班師，無以垂之千載。 朕仰惟遠祖，世居幽漠，違眾南遷，以享無窮之美，豈其無心，輕遺陵壤。 今之君子，寧獨有懷？ 當由天工人代、王業須成故也。 若不南鑾，即當移都於此，光宅土中，機亦時矣，王公等以為何如？ 議之所決，不得旋踵，欲遷者左，不欲者右。 」安定王休等相率如右。 前南安王楨進曰：[13]「夫愚者闇於成事，智者見於未萌。 行至德者不議於俗，成大功者不謀於眾，非常之人乃能建非常之事。 [14]廓神都以延王業，度土中以制帝京，周公啟之於前，陛下行之於後，故其宜也。 且天下至重，莫若皇居，人之所貴，寧如遺體？ 請上安聖躬，下慰民望，光宅中原，輟彼南伐。 此臣等願言，蒼生幸甚。 」羣臣咸唱「萬歲」。
When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made General-in-Chief of State Support and commanded the host in flank escort. From the departure from the capital until Luoyang, unceasing downpours persisted, yet an edict still ordered the six armies to set out. The Emperor, in martial dress, took the whip and rode forth. The officials bowed their foreheads before his horse's head. The Emperor said: "The plan for a long advance and the calculations in the ancestral temple are already settled. Now the great army is about to march — what more do you wish to say? "Chong stepped forward and said: "We your ministers have been unable to break the enemy within the command tent and govern the four seas from our seats, yet south of us a usurper holds a stolen title — truly this is our fault. Your Majesty, because the civil order and imperial roads are not yet unified, personally labors with the sacred carriage. We truly wish to exhaust our bodies and spend our lives, dying in the field of battle. Yet since leaving the capital there has been incessant rain; men and horses are weary and depleted. The road ahead is still far, and the floods are now severe. Moreover, within the Yi and Luo region even small streams still cause trouble — how much more the vast Yangzi River, which lies beyond our southern frontier? If we must build boats and oars, we shall have to halt. The army will age, provisions will run short, advance and retreat will both be difficult. To show pity in mourning and turn the banners homeward would be right by principle. The Emperor said: "The wish for unification — I have already stated it fully before. You take the rain as the difficulty, yet the seasons are in some measure knowable. How so? Summer having been scorching and dry, autumn therefore brings much rain. At the start of deep winter, the skies will surely clear. Within the next ten days or so,[12] if rain still does not cease, that will be Heaven's doing; but if the skies clear by then, marching will do no harm. In antiquity "do not campaign against a state in mourning" referred to feudal lords of the same roads — not to the king's text of unification. Having come this far, how can we halt the carriage? "Chong stepped forward again: "This present undertaking is what the realm does not wish for — only Your Majesty desires it. Emperor Wen of Han said, "Shall I alone ride a thousand-li horse — where would that lead?" I have the intent but not the words; I dare beg with my life. The Emperor said in great anger: "I am just setting out to order the universe and unify the realm, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great plan. The axe and punishment stand ready — speak no more! "He spurred his horse and was about to depart. Thereupon the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding Xiu, and the Concurrent Left Deputy Director, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, among others, all earnestly remonstrated with tears. The Emperor then addressed the officials: "This undertaking is no small matter. If we move and achieve nothing, how shall we show posterity? If we wish to withdraw the army, there is nothing to hand down through a thousand years. Reflecting on our distant ancestors who dwelt in the wild north, they went against the multitude and migrated south to enjoy boundless blessings — was it that they had no heart for the old tombs and lightly abandoned their ancestral land? Do gentlemen today alone cherish such thoughts? Surely it is because Heaven entrusts work to men and the royal enterprise must be completed. If we do not march south, then we must move the capital here, making our luminous abode in the Middle Land — the moment is timely. Princes and dukes, what do you think? The decision of this deliberation brooks no delay: those who wish to move, to the left; those who do not, to the right. "Prince of Anding Xiu and the others in succession went to the right. Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward:[13] "The foolish are blind to completed affairs; the wise see what has not yet sprouted. One who walks in supreme virtue does not debate with the vulgar; one who completes a great achievement does not consult the multitude. Only an extraordinary man can accomplish an extraordinary deed. [14]To broaden the divine capital and extend the royal enterprise, to measure the Middle Land and establish the imperial seat — the Duke of Zhou opened the way before, Your Majesty walks it after; therefore it is fitting. Moreover, nothing under Heaven is weightier than the imperial residence; what men hold dear — is it not like their own bodies left behind? We beg that above, the sacred person be secured; below, the people's hopes be soothed; that the luminous abode be in the Central Plain, and the southern campaign be set aside. This is what we your ministers wish to say — the common people would be greatly blessed. "The officials all cried "Long may he live ten thousand years!"
39
高祖初謀南遷，恐眾心戀舊，乃示為大舉，因以脅定羣情，外名南伐，其實遷也。 舊人懷土，多所不願，內憚南征，無敢言者，於是定都洛陽。 沖言於高祖曰：「陛下方修周公之制，定鼎成周。 然營建六寢，不可遊駕待就； 興築城郛，難以馬上營訖。 願暫還北都，令臣下經造，功成事訖，然後備文物之章，和玉鑾之響，巡時南徙，軌儀土中。 」高祖曰：「朕將巡省方岳，至鄴小停，春始便還，未宜遂不歸北。 」尋以沖為鎮南將軍，侍中、少傅如故，委以營構之任。 改封陽平郡開國侯，邑戶如先。
When the Emperor first planned the southern move of the capital, fearing that minds would cling to the old seat, he displayed a great campaign in order to coerce and fix the officials' minds — outwardly named a southern expedition, in truth a relocation. The old families, attached to their land, largely did not wish it; inwardly they feared the southern campaign but none dared speak. Thereupon the capital was fixed at Luoyang. Chong said to the Emperor: "Your Majesty is just now enacting the Duke of Zhou's institutions and fixing the sacred tripod at Chengzhou. Yet the six palaces cannot be built while the imperial carriage waits idle; raising walls and ramparts cannot be finished from horseback. We beg to return temporarily to the northern capital, let your ministers carry out the construction, and when the work is complete and affairs settled, then array the insignia of civilization, harmonize the jade bells of the imperial carriage, and at the proper season move south to take up the ceremonial standards in the Middle Land. The Emperor said: "I shall tour and inspect the sacred mountains. I shall stop briefly at Ye; at the start of spring I shall return — it is not yet fitting to resolve never to go back north. "Soon thereafter Chong was made General Who Guards the South; his posts as Palace Attendant and Junior Tutor remained as before, and he was entrusted with the task of construction. His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yangping Commandery with a fief of households as before.
40
車駕南伐，以沖兼左僕射，留守洛陽。 車駕渡淮，別詔安南大將軍元英、平南將軍劉藻討漢中，召雍涇岐三州兵六千人擬戍南鄭，克城則遣。 沖表諫曰：「秦州險阨，地接羌夷，自西師出後，餉援連續，加氐胡叛逆，所在奔命，運糧擐甲，迄茲未已。 今復豫差戍卒，懸擬山外，雖加優復，恐猶驚駭，脫終攻不克，徒動民情，連胡結夷，事或難測。 輒依旨密下刺史，待軍克鄭城，然後差遣，如臣愚見，猶謂未足。 何者？ 西道險阨，單徑千里，今欲深戍絕界之外，孤據羣賊之中，[15]敵攻不可卒援，食盡不可運糧。 古人有言，『雖鞭之長，不及馬腹』，南鄭於國，實為馬腹也。 且昔人攻伐，或城降而不取； 仁君用師，或撫民而遺地。 且王者之舉，情在拯民； 夷寇所守，意在惜地。 校之二義，德有淺深。 惠聲已遠，何遽於一城哉？ 且魏境所掩，九州過八，民人所臣，十分而九。 所未民者，惟漠北之與江外耳。 羈之在近，豈急急於今日也？ 宜待大開疆宇，廣拔城聚，多積資糧，食足支敵，然後置邦樹將，為吞并之舉。 今鍾離、壽陽，密邇未拔； 赭城、新野，跬步弗降。 [16]所克者舍之而不取，所降者撫之而旋戮。 東道既未可以近力守，西蕃寧可以遠兵固？ 若果欲置者，臣恐終以資敵也。 又今建都土中，地接寇壤，方須大收死士，平蕩江會。 輕遣單寡，棄令陷沒，恐後舉之日，眾以留守致懼，求其死効，未易可獲。 推此而論，不戍為上。 」高祖從之。
When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made Concurrent Left Deputy Director and left to guard Luoyang. When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai, a separate edict ordered the General Who Pacifies the South, Yuan Ying, and the General Who Levels the South, Liu Zao, to attack Hanzhong, and summoned six thousand troops from Yong, Jing, and Qi Provinces to garrison Nanzheng — to be dispatched once the city was taken. Chong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Qinzhou is rugged and defensible, its land bordering the Qiang and barbarians. Since the western army set out, supplies and reinforcements have flowed unceasingly. Added to this, the Di and Hu have rebelled; everywhere men run at the call to arms. Transporting grain and donning armor — to this day it has not ceased. Now to pre-assign garrison troops, poised beyond the mountains — even with added exemptions and relief, I fear the people will still be alarmed. If the attack ultimately fails, we will have stirred the populace for nothing; linking Hu with barbarians, affairs may become hard to foresee. I have already followed the edict and secretly instructed the provincial governors: once the army takes Zheng City, then dispatch the troops. Yet in my humble view, even this still falls short. Why? The western route is rugged; a single path stretches a thousand li. Now you wish to garrison deeply beyond the farthest border, isolated among bandits,[15] where enemy attack cannot quickly be relieved and when food runs out grain cannot be transported. The ancients said, "Though the whip is long, it does not reach the horse's belly." Nanzheng to the state is truly the horse's belly. Moreover, when men of old campaigned, sometimes a city surrendered and they did not take it; a benevolent ruler used his army and sometimes comforted the people while leaving the land behind. The purpose of a king's enterprise lies in saving the people; what barbarian raiders hold to is cherishing land. Weighing the two principles, virtue has its depths and shallows. Our benevolent name already reaches far — why rush after a single city? Moreover, the Wei domain covers more than eight of the Nine Provinces; of the people who submit, nine parts in ten. Those not yet subject are only the far north of the desert and the lands beyond the Yangzi. To hold them loosely when they are near — must this be rushed today? We ought to wait until the borders are greatly opened, cities and settlements widely taken, resources and grain abundantly stored, provisions sufficient to sustain the enemy — then establish provinces and appoint generals for a campaign of annexation. Now Zhongli and Shouyang lie close yet are not taken; Zhe City and Xinye, a short step away, have not submitted. [16]What we take we abandon rather than hold; those who submit we comfort and then execute. If the eastern route cannot yet be held with nearby strength, can the western frontier truly be secured with distant troops? If you truly intend to garrison it, I fear in the end it will only supply the enemy. Moreover, now that the capital is established in the Middle Land, our territory borders the enemy — we need urgently to gather resolute warriors and sweep clean the Yangzi junction. To lightly send a small, isolated force and abandon it to defeat — I fear that when the next campaign comes, the troops, fearful because of those left to garrison, will be hard to move to die in earnest service. Reasoning from this, not garrisoning is best. The Emperor followed his advice.
41
車駕還都，引見沖等，謂之曰：「本所以多置官者，慮有令僕闇弱，百事稽壅，若明獨聰專，則權勢大併。 [17]今朕雖不得為聰明，又不為劣闇，卿等不為大賢，亦不為大惡。 且可一兩年許，少置官司。」
When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, the Emperor received Chong and the others and said to them: "The reason for establishing so many offices was the fear that some Director or Deputy Director might be dull and weak, and a hundred affairs become blocked. If one man alone were brilliant and shrewd, power would largely be combined. [17]Now I am neither able to be brilliantly wise, nor am I inferior and dull; you are neither greatly virtuous nor greatly wicked. For a year or two, let us establish fewer offices."
42
高祖自鄴還京，汎舟洪池，乃從容謂沖曰：「朕欲從此通渠於洛，南伐之日，何容不從此入洛，從洛入河，從河入汴，從汴入清，以至於淮？ 下船而戰，猶出戶而鬬，此乃軍國之大計。 今溝渠若須二萬人以下、六十日有成者，宜以漸修之。 」沖對曰：「若爾，便是士無遠涉之勞，戰有兼人之力。 」遷尚書僕射，仍領少傅。 改封清淵縣開國侯，邑戶如前。 乃太子恂廢，沖罷少傅。
When the Emperor returned from Ye to the capital, he floated a boat on Hong Pool and then calmly said to Chong: "I wish to open a canal from here to Luoyang. On the day of the southern campaign, how could we fail to enter Luoyang from here, enter the river from Luoyang, enter the Bian from the river, enter the Qing from the Bian, until we reach the Huai? To disembark and fight is like stepping out the door to battle — this is a great plan for army and state. If a canal now requires fewer than twenty thousand men and can be completed in sixty days, it should be built gradually." Chong replied: "If so, then troops would be spared the toil of long marches, and in battle they would have the strength of more than one man." He was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, still retaining the Junior Tutorship. His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Qingyuan County with a fief of households as before. When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Chong was removed from the Junior Tutorship.
43
高祖引見公卿於清徽堂，高祖曰：「聖人之大寶，惟位與功，是以功成作樂，治定制禮。 今徙極中天，創居嵩洛，雖大構未成，要自條紀略舉。 但南有未賓之豎，兼兇蠻密邇，朕夙夜悵惋，良在於茲。 取南之計決矣，朕行之謀必矣。 若依近代也，則天子下帷深宮之內； 準上古也，則有親行，祚延七百。 [18]魏晉不征，旋踵而殞，祚之修短，在德不在征。 今但以行期未知早晚。 知幾其神乎，朕既非神，焉能知也。 而頃來陰陽卜術之士，咸勸朕今征必克。 此既家國大事，宜共君臣各盡所見，不得以朕先言，便致依違，退有同異。 」沖對曰：「夫征戰之法，先之人事，然後卜筮，今卜筮雖吉，猶恐人事未備。 今年秋稔，有損常實，又京師始遷，眾業未定，加之征戰，以為未可。 宜至來秋。 」高祖曰：「僕射之言，非為不合。 朕意之所慮，乃有社稷之憂。 然咫尺寇戎，無宜自安，理須如此。 僕射言人事未從，亦不必如此。 朕去十七年，擁二十萬眾，行不出畿甸，此人事之盛，而非天時。 往年乘機，天時乃可，而闕人事，又致不捷。 若待人事備，復非天時，若之何？ 如僕射之言，便終無征理。 朕若秋行無克捷，三君子並付司寇。 不可不人盡其心。 」罷議而出。
The Emperor received the princes and officials at the Qingwei Hall and said: "The great treasure of the sage is position and achievement; therefore when achievement is complete one makes music, and when governance is settled one fixes ritual. Now we have moved the capital to the center of Heaven, newly established our seat at Song and Luo. Though the great construction is not yet complete, the basic order must in general be set forth. But in the south there are unsubmissive rebels, and fierce barbarians press close at hand. Day and night I grieve — truly the cause lies here. The plan to take the south is decided; my resolve to carry it out is firm. If one follows recent times, then the Son of Heaven sits behind lowered curtains deep within the palace; if one follows high antiquity, then there is personal campaigning, and the throne endured seven hundred years. [18]Wei and Jin did not campaign and swiftly perished; the length of a throne's endurance lies in virtue, not in campaigning. Now it is only that the date of the march is not yet known, early or late. "To know the subtle before it appears — that is divine." I am not divine — how can I know? Yet lately the masters of yin-yang and divination have all urged that if we campaign now we shall surely prevail. This is a great affair of state and dynasty; ruler and ministers alike must each give their full view. You may not, because I have spoken first, then hesitate in assent or dissent in retreat. Chong replied: "In the method of campaigning, human affairs come first, and only afterward divination. Now though divination is auspicious, I still fear human affairs are not yet ready. This year's harvest falls short of the usual yield. The capital has just been moved and the people's livelihoods are not yet settled. To add a campaign on top of this — I do not think the time is right. It should wait until next autumn. The Emperor said: "What the Deputy Director says is not without reason. What I myself worry about is a concern for the altars of state. Yet the enemy is close at hand; it is not fitting to rest at ease. By principle it must be so. What the Deputy Director says about human affairs not being ready need not be taken so far. Seventeen years ago I led two hundred thousand men and marched without leaving the capital region — that was the greatness of human affairs, not the season of Heaven. In years past the season was favorable, yet because human affairs were lacking, victory was not achieved. If we wait until human affairs are ready, it will no longer be the season of Heaven — what then? By what the Deputy Director says, there would finally be no grounds for campaigning at all. If I campaign in autumn and there is no victory, the three of you will all be handed over to the Minister of Justice. Each of you must not fail to give your full heart." The deliberation ended and he withdrew.
44
後世宗為太子，高祖醼於清徽堂。 高祖曰：「皇儲所以纂歷三才，光昭七祖，斯乃億兆咸悅，天人同泰，故延卿就此一醼，以暢忻情。 」高祖又曰：「天地之道，一盈一虛，豈有常泰。 天道猶爾，況人事乎？ 故有升有黜，自古而然。 悼往欣今，良用深歎。 」沖對曰：「東暉承儲，蒼生咸幸。 但臣前忝師傅，弗能弼諧，仰慚天日，慈造寬含，得預此醼，慶愧交深。 」高祖曰：「朕尚弗能革其昏，師傅何勞愧謝也。」
Later, when Shizong became Crown Prince, the Emperor held a banquet at the Qingwei Hall. The Emperor said: "The Crown Prince exists to inherit the three powers and glorify the seven ancestors. This is what makes the myriad people rejoice and Heaven and man share felicity. Therefore I have invited you to this banquet to give full vent to our joy. The Emperor also said: "The way of Heaven and Earth is one fullness and one emptiness — how could there be constant prosperity? If the way of Heaven is so, how much more human affairs? Therefore there is promotion and there is dismissal — it has been so since antiquity. Mourning the past and rejoicing in the present — truly I sigh deeply. Chong replied: "The Eastern Splendor inherits the succession; the common people are all blessed. But I formerly served as tutor and failed to assist and harmonize. Looking up, I am ashamed before sun and sky; yet Your Majesty's gracious creation was broad and forgiving, allowing me to join this banquet — joy and shame mingle deeply. The Emperor said: "I am still unable to reform his dullness — why should the tutor trouble himself with apologies?"
45
後尚書疑元拔、穆泰罪事，沖奏曰：「前彭城鎮將元拔與穆泰同逆，養子降壽宜從拔罪。 而太尉、咸陽王禧等，以為律文養子而為罪，父及兄弟不知情者不坐。 謹審律意，以養子於父非天性，於兄弟非同氣，敦薄既差，故刑典有降，是以養子雖為罪，而父兄不預。 然父兄為罪，養子不知謀，易地均情，豈獨從戮乎？ 理固不然。 臣以為：依據律文，不追戮於所生，則從坐於所養，[19]明矣。 又律惟言父不從子，不稱子不從父，[20]當是優尊厲卑之義。 臣禧等以為：『律雖不正見，互文起制，於乞也舉父之罪，於養也見子坐，是為互起。 互起兩明，無罪必矣。 若以嫡繼養與生同，則父子宜均，祇明不坐。 且繼養之注云：若有別制，不同此律。 又令文云：諸有封爵，若無親子，及其身卒，雖有養繼，國除不襲。 是為有福不及己，有罪便預坐。 均事等情，律令之意，便相矛盾。 伏度律旨，必不然也。 』臣沖以為：指例條尋，罪在無疑，準令語情，頗亦同式。 」詔曰：「僕射之議，據律明矣； 太尉等論，於典矯也。 [21]養所以從戮者，緣其已免所生，故不得復甄於所養。 此獨何福，長處吞舟？ 于國所以不襲者，重列爵，特立制，因天之所絕，推而除之耳，豈復報對刑賞？ 于斯則應死，可特原之。」
Later, when the Ministry of Justice questioned the guilt of Yuan Ba and Mu Tai, Chong submitted a memorial: "Formerly the garrison commander of Pengcheng, Yuan Ba, joined Mu Tai in rebellion. The adopted son Jiang Shou should share Ba's guilt. But the Grand Commandant, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and others held that the law states: when an adopted son commits a crime, if the father and brothers did not know, they are not punished. Carefully examining the intent of the law: between an adopted son and the father there is no natural bond; between him and brothers there is no shared breath. Since the bond of affection is thinner, the penal code accordingly reduces punishment. Therefore though an adopted son commits a crime, father and brothers are not implicated. Yet if the father and brothers commit a crime and the adopted son did not know the plot, by the same principle applied in reverse, should he alone be executed? By principle this surely cannot be so. I hold that according to the letter of the law, one is not pursued for punishment at the place of birth, but one is implicated at the place of adoption —[19] this is clear. Moreover the law speaks only of the father not following the son, not of the son not following the father —[20] this must be the meaning of honoring the superior and restraining the inferior. Minister Xi and others hold: "Though the law does not state it directly, cross-text establishes the rule: in the case of begging for adoption it cites the father's crime; in the case of adoption it shows the son's punishment — this is mutual establishment. When both sides are mutually established, innocence is certain. If one treats legitimate succession by adoption as the same as birth, then father and son should be equal — it need only state clearly that they are not punished. Moreover the commentary on succession by adoption says: if there is a separate statute, it differs from this law. Moreover the ordinance states: for all who hold enfeoffment, if there is no natural son, when they themselves die, though there is an adopted successor, the fief is abolished and not inherited. This means that blessings do not reach oneself, but guilt is immediately shared in punishment. Equalizing affairs and equalizing sentiment, the intent of law and ordinance then contradict each other. Reflecting on the intent of the law, it surely cannot be so. "Minister Chong holds: citing precedents and searching the articles, guilt is beyond doubt; matching the ordinance to the sentiment of the language, it is also largely of the same form. An edict said: "The Deputy Director's reasoning, according to the law, is clear; the Grand Commandant's discussion twists the canon." [21] An adopted son is executed because, once spared on account of his birth father, he cannot again be exempted through his adoptive family. Why should this one alone enjoy such favor, forever escaping the law that catches even great offenders? The reason a fief is not inherited is that noble rank is weighty and a separate statute was established: when Heaven cuts off a line, the state removes it by decree — that is hardly a matter of reciprocal criminal reward and punishment. In this case he deserves death, but he may be specially pardoned."
46
沖機敏有巧思，北京明堂、圓丘、太廟，及洛都初基，安處郊兆，新起堂寢，皆資於沖。 勤志強力，孜孜無怠，旦理文簿，兼營匠制，几案盈積，剞劂在手，終不勞厭也。 然顯貴門族，務益六姻，兄弟子姪，皆有爵官，一家歲祿，萬匹有餘，是其親者，雖復癡聾，無不超越官次。 時論亦以此少之。
Quick-witted and full of ingenious ideas, Chong designed the Bright Hall, Circular Mound, and Grand Ancestral Temple in the northern capital, and when Luoyang was first laid out he planned the suburban altars and new halls and chambers. Diligent and tireless, he handled documents by day while directing craftsmen as well; with desks piled high and carving knife in hand, he never wearied of the work. Yet as a prominent noble house they enriched all six degrees of kin: brothers, sons, and nephews all held titles and offices, and the family's annual stipend exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk. Even dull or deaf relatives were promoted above their proper rank. Contemporary opinion faulted him for this as well.
47
年纔四十，而鬢髮班白，姿貌豐美，未有衰狀。 李彪之入京也，孤微寡援，而自立不羣，以沖好士，傾心宗附。 沖亦重其器學，禮而納焉，每言之於高祖，公私共相援益。 及彪為中尉、兼尚書，為高祖知待，便謂非復藉沖，而更相輕背，惟公坐斂袂而已，無復宗敬之意也。 沖頗銜之。 後高祖南征，沖與吏部尚書、任城王澄並以彪倨傲無禮，遂禁止之。 奏其罪狀，沖手自作，家人不知，辭甚激切，因以自劾。 高祖覽其表，歎悵者久之，既而曰：「道固可謂溢也，僕射亦為滿矣。 」沖時震怒，[22]數數責彪前後愆悖，瞋目大呼，投折几案。 盡收御史，皆泥首面縛，詈辱肆口。 沖素性溫柔，而一旦暴恚，遂發病荒悸，言語亂錯，猶扼腕叫詈，稱李彪小人。 醫藥所不能療，或謂肝藏傷裂。 旬有餘日而卒，時年四十九。 高祖為舉哀於懸瓠，發聲悲泣，不能自勝。 詔曰：「沖貞和資性，德義樹身，訓業自家，道素形國。 太和之始，朕在弱齡，早委機密，實康時務。 鴻漸瀍洛，朝選開清，升冠端右，惟允出納。 忠肅柔明，足敷睿範，仁恭信惠，有結民心。 可謂國之賢也，朝之望也。 方昇寵秩，以旌功舊，奄致喪逝，悲痛于懷。 既留勤應陟，兼良宿宜褒，可贈司空公，給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲，贈錢三十萬、布五百匹、蠟二百斤。 」有司奏諡曰文穆。 葬於覆舟山，近杜預冢，高祖之意也。 後車駕自鄴還洛，路經沖墓，左右以聞，高祖臥疾望墳，掩泣久之。 詔曰：「司空文穆公，德為時宗，勳簡朕心，不幸徂逝，託墳邙嶺，旋鑾覆舟，躬睇塋域，悲仁惻舊，有慟朕衷。 可遣太牢之祭，以申吾懷。 」及與留京百官相見，皆敍沖亡沒之故，言及流淚。 高祖得留臺啟，知沖患狀，謂右衞宋弁曰：「僕射執我樞衡，總釐朝務，清儉居躬，知寵已久。 朕以仁明忠雅，委以台司之寄，使我出境無後顧之憂，一朝忽有此患，朕甚懷愴慨。 」其相痛惜如此。
Though only forty, his temples were already streaked with white; his bearing remained full and handsome, with no sign of decline. When Li Biao came to the capital he was isolated and without backing, yet stood apart from the crowd; because Chong favored talented men, Biao devoted himself to him and joined his circle. Chong also valued his talent and learning, received him with courtesy, and commended him to Emperor Gaozu; in public and private they supported and benefited one another. Once Biao became Commandant of Justice and concurrent Minister of the Masters of Writing and won the emperor's trust, he decided he no longer needed Chong; they grew mutually disdainful and estranged, and at court Biao merely drew in his sleeves, showing no further reverence for his former patron. Chong deeply resented this. Later, when the emperor marched south, Chong and Minister of the Civil Office Prince Cheng of Rencheng charged Biao with arrogance and lack of courtesy and had him detained. He submitted the charges in a memorial Chong wrote in his own hand, without his household's knowledge; the language was very sharp, and he thereby impeached himself as well. When the emperor read the memorial he sighed regretfully for a long time, then said, "The Way can indeed be said to overflow — and the Vice Director is also full." Chong was then furious; [22] again and again he reproached Biao for his successive faults and insolence, glaring and shouting and hurling desks until they broke. He seized all the censors, had them kneel with mud-smeared faces and bound hands, and reviled them at will. Gentle by nature, Chong in one sudden fit of rage fell ill with delirium and palpitations; his speech became confused, yet he still clutched his wrist and shouted curses, calling Li Biao a petty man. Medicine could not cure him; some said his liver had been ruptured. After a little more than ten days he died, at the age of forty-nine. The emperor held mourning for him at Xuanhuo, weeping aloud in grief beyond self-control. An edict said, "Chong's nature was upright and harmonious; he rooted himself in virtue and righteousness, trained in learning within his family, and his conduct shaped the state. At the beginning of the Taihe reign, when I was still young, I early entrusted him with confidential affairs, and he truly brought order to the affairs of the age. When the great enterprise advanced to the Chan and Luo rivers, court selection opened and became clear; he rose to the foremost place on the right and was truly fit to receive and deliver imperial business. Loyal, reverent, gentle, and bright, he fully embodied the sage's model; benevolent, respectful, faithful, and gracious, he won the people's hearts. He may be called a worthy man of the state and the hope of the court. Just as he was to rise in favor and rank to honor his long service, he suddenly passed away, and grief fills my breast. Having long shown diligence deserving promotion, and being a fine elder worthy of praise, he is posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works, granted the secret funerary objects of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing, with thirty thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred catties of wax given in gift. The responsible offices memorialized that his posthumous title should be Wenmu. He was buried on Mount Fuzhou, near the tomb of Du Yu — at the emperor's wish. Later, when the imperial carriage returned from Ye to Luoyang and passed Chong's tomb, those around him reported it; the ailing emperor looked toward the grave from his couch and wept, covering his face, for a long time. An edict said, "Duke Wenmu of the Ministry of Works was a moral exemplar of the age; his merit is inscribed on my heart. Sadly he has passed away; his tomb rests on the Mang Ridge. Now the carriage turns at Mount Fuzhou, and I myself gaze upon the graveyard — pity for his benevolence stirs old feeling, and my innermost heart is stricken." A grand sacrificial offering may be sent to express my feelings. When he met with the officials who had remained in the capital, he recounted the circumstances of Chong's death, and spoke until tears flowed. When the emperor received the capital memorial reporting Chong's illness, he said to Song Bian of the Right Guard, "The Vice Director held my pivot and balance, overseeing the affairs of court; he lived plainly and frugally in person, and I have long known his favor. Because he was benevolent, bright, loyal, and refined, I entrusted him with the charge of the Secretariat, so that when I went beyond the borders I had no worry for what lay behind; suddenly one morning this affliction arose — I am deeply grieved and indignant." Such was the depth of their mutual sorrow and esteem.
48
沖兄弟六人，四母所出，頗相忿䦧。 及沖之貴，封祿恩賜皆以共之，內外輯睦。 父亡後同居二十餘年，至洛乃別第宅，更相友愛，久無間然。 皆沖之德也。 始沖之見私寵也，兄子韶恒有憂色，慮致傾敗。 後榮名日顯，稍乃自安。 而沖明目當官，圖為己任，自始迄終，無所避屈。 其體時推運，皆此類也。 子延寔等，語在外戚傳。
Chong had six brothers, born of four mothers, and they were rather mutually resentful. When Chong rose to eminence, enfeoffments, stipends, and imperial gifts were all shared with them, and inside and outside the family they lived in harmony. After their father's death they lived together for more than twenty years; only when they reached Luoyang did they separate into different residences, yet they became still more mutually affectionate, and for long there was no estrangement. All this was Chong's virtue. When Chong first received private favor, his elder brother's son Shao always wore a worried look, fearing a fall to ruin. Later, as glory and fame grew daily, he gradually became at ease. Yet Chong saw clearly in office and took responsibility as his own task; from beginning to end he never evaded or yielded. His grasp of the times and promotion of fortune were all of this kind. His sons Yanshi and others — their accounts are in the biography of the empresses' kin.
49
史臣曰：燕趙信多奇士。 李孝伯風範鑒略，蓋亦過人遠甚。 世祖雄猜嚴斷，崔浩已見誅夷，而入參心膂，出幹政事，獻可替否，無際可尋，故能從容任遇，以功名始卒。 其智器固以優乎？ 安世識具通雅，時幹之良。 瑒以豪俊達，郁則儒博顯。 李沖早延寵眷，入幹腹心，風流識業，固乃一時之秀。 終協契聖主，佐命太和，位當端揆，身任梁棟，德洽家門，功著王室。 蓋有魏之亂臣也。
The historian says: Yan and Zhao truly produce many extraordinary men. Li Xiaobo's bearing, discernment, and strategy also surpassed other men by far. Emperor Shizu was fierce, suspicious, strict, and decisive; Cui Hao had already been executed, yet Xiaobo entered to share in the ruler's innermost counsels and went out to manage government affairs, offering approval or criticism without any gap to be found — thus he could meet favor at ease and maintain merit and fame from beginning to end. Was his intelligence and capacity not indeed superior? Anshi's discernment was comprehensive, refined, and elegant — a fine man of the age in government affairs. Yang distinguished himself through bold talent; Yu was eminent through broad Confucian learning. Li Chong early won imperial favor, entered to serve at the ruler's inmost heart, and in bearing, talent, discernment, and achievement was truly a leading figure of the age. In the end he joined in accord with the sage ruler, assisted the Taihe enterprise, stood at the head of the chief ministers, bore the role of a beam and pillar, spread virtue through his household, and made his merit shine in the royal house. He was, one may say, a pillar minister of Wei.
50

校勘記
Collation Notes
52
宣世祖詔勞問義恭等諸本「等」訛「率」，不可通，今據北史卷三三李孝伯傳、冊府卷六六０ 〈七八九四頁〉 改。
"Emperor Shizu issued an edict commending and inquiring after Yigong and the others": all editions corrupt "and the others" as "lead"; the text is untenable; restored according to Beishi, juan 33, biography of Li Xiaobo, and Cefu, juan 660 (p. 7894) Corrected.
53
眾無三旅始濟翮水冊府卷六六０宋本同，明本 〈七八九六頁〉 「三」作「一」。 按宋書卷五九張暢傳也作「一」，據文義作「一」是。 又冊府 〈同上卷頁〉 及宋書張暢傳「翮水」並作「融水」。 檢宋書卷七二南平王鑠傳，云：「鑠遣參軍胡盛之出汝南、上蔡，向長社。 」汝潁一帶不聞有翮水或融水，疑有誤。
"The force had not three companies when they began crossing the He River": Cefu, juan 660, Song edition agrees; Ming edition (p. 7896) reads "three" as "one." Song Shu, juan 59, biography of Zhang Chang, also has "one"; according to the sense of the passage, "one" is correct. Also Cefu (same juan and page) and Song Shu, biography of Zhang Chang, both read "He River" as "Rong River." Checking Song Shu, juan 72, biography of Prince Shuo of Nanping, it says, "Shuo sent his aide Hu Shengzhi out from Runan and Shangcai toward Changshe." In the Ru and Ying region one does not hear of a He River or Rong River; there is probably an error.
54
示使崔邪利撫之而已冊府 〈同上卷頁〉 、宋書卷五九張暢傳「示」作「亦」，較長。 作「示」亦通，今不改。
"Only show and have Cui Xieli pacify them": Cefu (same juan and page) and Song Shu, juan 59, biography of Zhang Chang, read "show" as "also," which is longer. Reading "show" is also intelligible; the text is not changed.
55
興安二年出為使持節散騎常侍平西將軍秦州刺史墓誌集釋肅宗充華盧令媛墓誌 〈圖版三七〉 稱祖淵，「夫人趙郡李氏，父孝伯，散騎常侍、尚書、使持節、平西將軍、泰州刺史、宣城公」。 集釋卷二歷引錢大昕以來諸家之說，證地形志 〈卷一０六下〉 治蒲坂之秦州為泰州之訛，並以此傳「秦州」亦「泰州」之訛。 按此「秦州」當作「泰州」。 但傳文無治蒲坂明文，今不改。
In the second year of Xing'an he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Qin Province: Epigraphical Collection and Commentary, epitaph of Lady Lu Lingyuan, Consort of Emperor Suzong (Plate 37) calls the grandfather Yuan: "Lady Li of Zhao Commandery, father Xiaobo, Regular Attendant, Minister, Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Tai Province, Duke of Xuancheng." Collection and Commentary, juan 2, cites the views of Qian Daxin and later scholars to prove that in the Treatise on Geography (juan 106, Part 2) Qin Province administered at Puban is a corruption for Tai Province, and that "Qin Province" in this biography is also a corruption for "Tai Province." On examination, "Qin Province" should read "Tai Province." But the biography text has no explicit statement that it was administered at Puban; the text is not changed.
56
況先臣在蒙委任冊府卷八七五 〈一０三七三頁〉 「在」作「往」，疑是。
"Moreover, my late minister, while receiving appointment": Cefu, juan 875 (p. 10373) reads "while" as "formerly"; this is probably correct.
57
子安世諸本卷末殿本入考證，不注所出。 有宋人校語云：「高氏小史，魏書列傳第四十五高祐、崔挺、李安世三人。 其傳云：『李安世，趙郡人也。 宣城公孝伯之兄子，父祥，中書博士。 』今魏書諸本，祥及安世事皆附此卷孝伯傳後。 按李肇經史釋題、楊九齡經史目錄，第四十五卷高祐、崔挺、李安世三人。 宗諫史目、殷藏用十三代史目惟高祐、崔挺而無李安世。 此卷論安世及瑒、郁與北史同，疑李延壽用魏書舊語，後人移安世傳附孝伯，因取北史論安世父子事於此篇，亦不可考證。 故載之目錄同異，以備傳疑。」
"Son Anshi": all editions at the end of the juan; the Palace Edition enters it into textual verification without noting the source. There is a Song-dynasty collation note saying, "Gao's Brief History: Wei Shu Biography 45 contains Gao You, Cui Ting, and Li Anshi. Its biography says, 'Li Anshi was a man of Zhao Commandery. Nephew of Duke of Xuancheng Xiaobo; his father Xiang was a Doctor of the Secretariat.' In the various editions of Wei Shu today, the affairs of Xiang and Anshi are all appended after this juan's biography of Xiaobo. According to Li Zhao's Explanatory Titles of the Classics and Histories and Yang Jiuling's Catalogue of the Classics and Histories, juan 45 contains Gao You, Cui Ting, and Li Anshi. Zong Jian's Catalogue of Histories and Yin Cangyong's Catalogue of the Thirteen Dynastic Histories have only Gao You and Cui Ting, and not Li Anshi. This juan's appraisal of Anshi and of Yang and Yu agrees with Beishi; it is suspected that Li Yanshou used old language from Wei Shu, and that later men moved Anshi's biography to append it to Xiaobo's, then took Beishi's appraisal of Anshi and his sons for this chapter — this too cannot be verified. Therefore the differences in the catalogues are recorded to preserve the doubt in transmission."
58
三長既立冊府卷四九五 〈五九二四頁〉 「三長」作「子孫」。 按下文說由於李安世上疏「均田之制，起於此矣」。 均田制頒佈在太和九年 〈四八五〉 十月 〈見卷七上高祖紀上〉 ，安世上疏，必在其前。 而立三長却在太和十年二月 〈見卷七下高祖紀下〉 。 安世上疏時，尚未頒佈均田制，當然更沒有立三長。 疏中所謂「三長既立」，解釋不通。 疑作「子孫既立」是。
"The Three Chiefs system had already been established": Cefu, juan 495 (p. 5924) reads "Three Chiefs" as "descendants." The text below says that because Li Anshi submitted a memorial, "the equal-field system arose from this." The equal-field system was promulgated in the ninth year of Taihe (p. 485) in the tenth month (see Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu, Part 1, juan 7) Anshi's memorial must have come before that. Yet the establishment of the Three Chiefs came only in the second month of the tenth year of Taihe (see Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu, Part 2, juan 7) . When Anshi submitted his memorial, the equal-field system had not yet been promulgated, so of course the Three Chiefs had not yet been established. The phrase in the memorial, "the Three Chiefs system had already been established," cannot be explained. It is suspected that "descendants had already been established" is correct.
59
猶罰瑒金一兩諸本「猶」訛「獨」，今據北史卷三三李孝伯附李瑒傳、冊府卷五三０ 〈六三三五頁〉 改。
"Still fined Yang one liang of gold": all editions corrupt "still" as "alone"; restored according to Beishi, juan 33, biography of Li Xiaobo with appended biography of Li Yang, and Cefu, juan 530 (p. 6335) Corrected.
60
期年之中諸本「期」作「暮」，北史卷三三、冊府卷八五二 〈一０一二六頁〉 作「朞」。 「暮」乃「朞」字形近而訛，今據改，統一作「期」。
"Within the span of a full year": all editions read "period" as "twilight"; Beishi, juan 33, and Cefu, juan 852 (p. 10126) have "period." "Twilight" is a corruption through graphic similarity to "period"; the text is emended accordingly and uniformly reads "period."
61
永熙初除散騎常侍大將軍北史卷三三「大將軍」上有「衞」字。 按大將軍第一品，班在三公上 〈見卷一一三官氏志〉 ，與所除之散騎常侍、左光祿大夫、都官尚書等官品不相當。 且李郁死後贈驃騎大將軍，豈有生前已為大將軍之理。 這裏「大將軍」上當脫「衞」字。
At the beginning of Yongxi he was appointed Regular Attendant and Grand General: Beishi, juan 33, has the character "Guard" before "Grand General." Grand General is first rank, ranking above the Three Dukes (see Monograph on Offices and Clans, juan 113) , which does not match the ranks of the offices to which he was appointed — Regular Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Justice. Moreover, after Li Yu's death he was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Agile Cavalry — how could he already have been Grand General in life? Here the character "Guard" must be missing before "Grand General."
62
比後月十間冊府卷五四一 〈六四八五頁〉 「月十」作「十月」，疑是。
"Within the next ten months or so": Cefu, juan 541 (p. 6485) reads "month ten" as "tenth month"; this is probably correct.
63
前南安王楨進曰諸本無「前」字，北史卷三三李沖傳、冊府卷一三 〈一四八頁〉 有。 按卷一九下南安王楨傳，楨先以聚斂「削除官爵，禁錮終身」，後以議定遷都，復封。 這時王爵未復，故稱「前」。 冊府採魏書而與北史同，知這裏脫「前」字，今據補。
"Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward and said": all editions lack the character "former"; Beishi, juan 33, biography of Li Chong, and Cefu, juan 13 (p. 148) have it. According to juan 19, Part 2, biography of Prince Zhen of Nan'an: Zhen was first, for extortion, "stripped of office and rank and imprisoned for life," then restored to his fief for his part in deciding the transfer of the capital. At this time his princely title had not yet been restored, hence he is called "former." Cefu drew on Wei Shu and agrees with Beishi; knowing that "former" is missing here, it is now supplied accordingly.
64
非常之人乃能建非常之事諸本「乃能」下脫「建」字，今據冊府卷一三 〈一四八頁〉 補。
"Only extraordinary men can accomplish extraordinary deeds": all editions omit the character "establish" after "can"; restored according to Cefu, juan 13 (p. 148) Supplied.
65
孤據羣賊之中諸本「中」作「口」，冊府卷五三０ 〈六三二七頁〉 、通鑑卷一四０ 〈四三八三頁〉 並作「中」。 按「中」和上「深戍絕界之外」相對，「口」字訛，今據改。
"Alone holding out among a host of bandits": all editions read "among" as "mouth"; Cefu, juan 530 (p. 6327) and Zizhi tongjian, juan 140 (p. 4383) all have "among." "Among" corresponds above to "deep garrisons beyond the frontier boundary"; the character "mouth" is corrupt; the text is emended accordingly.
66
赭城新野跬步弗降諸本「赭」作「諸」，通鑑卷一四０ 〈四三八三頁〉 作「赭」，考異不言有異文。 按卷一０六中地形志中南青州東莞郡有諸縣，也即漢琅邪郡的諸縣，故城在今山東諸城縣西南。 其地自皇興三年 〈四六九〉 慕容白曜取青州後，久屬北魏，不得云「跬步弗降」。 「赭城」即赭陽 〈見通鑑胡注〉 ，和新野都是南齊邊界要地，太和二十一年 〈四九七〉 元宏親自統軍南下，赭陽、新野始被攻佔 〈見卷七下高祖紀下〉 。 這裏「諸」字顯為「赭」字形訛，今據通鑑改。
"Zhecheng and Xinye did not submit at every step": all editions read "Zhe" as "Zhu"; Zizhi tongjian, juan 140 (p. 4383) has "Zhe"; Kaoyi does not note variant readings. According to juan 106, Part 2, Treatise on Geography, Southern Qing Province, Dongguan Commandery has Zhu County — that is, the Zhu County of Han's Langye Commandery; its old city is southwest of present-day Zhucheng County in Shandong. That region, from the third year of Huangxing (p. 469) after Murong Baiyao took Qing Province, long belonged to Northern Wei — one cannot say "did not submit at every step." "Zhecheng" is Zheyang (see Hu annotation to Zizhi tongjian) , and Xinye were both key places on the Southern Qi frontier; in the twenty-first year of Taihe (p. 497) Yuan Hong personally commanded the army south; only then were Zheyang and Xinye captured (see Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu, Part 2, juan 7) . Here the character "Zhu" is clearly a graphic corruption of "Zhe"; the text is emended according to Zizhi tongjian.
67
若明獨聰專則權勢大併冊府卷四六 〈五二二頁〉 此句作「若明，則聽斷獨專； 聰，則權勢大併」，語意較明白，疑傳本訛脫。
"If clear, alone, perceptive, and exclusive, then power and authority greatly merge": Cefu, juan 46 (p. 522) This sentence reads, "If clear, then judgment and decision are exclusively one's own; if perceptive, then power and authority greatly merge" — the sense is clearer; the transmitted text is suspected of corruption and omission.
68
準上古也則有親行祚延七百冊府卷五七 〈六三四頁〉 「親行」上有「周武」二字。 按「周武親行，祚延七百」與下「魏晉不征，旋踵而殞」相對。 「則有」下當有脫文，冊府殘存「周武」二字，但所脫不止此，「則有」下當有與上句「天子下帷深宮之內」作對的幾個字，然後接「周武親征」云云。
"Matching antiquity, then there is personal campaigning and the throne endures seven hundred years": Cefu, juan 57 (p. 634) Above "personal campaigning" are the two characters "Zhou Wu." "Zhou Wu campaigned in person, and the throne endured seven hundred years" corresponds below to "Wei and Jin did not campaign, and perished in the turning of a heel." Below "then there is" there must be missing text; Cefu preserves the two characters "Zhou Wu," but what is missing is not limited to this — below "then there is" there should be several characters parallel to the line above, "the Son of Heaven within the deep palace with curtains lowered," and then "Zhou Wu campaigned in person" and so on.
69
不追戮於所生則從坐於所養諸本「追」上無「不」字。 冊府卷六一五 〈七三九一頁〉 有。 按李沖意謂據律文，養子不因生父犯罪而連坐，那麼養父犯罪就該連坐。 無「不」字不可通，今據補。
"Not pursuing execution through the birth father, then implicated through the adoptive family": all editions lack the character "not" before "pursue." Cefu, juan 615 (p. 7391) has it. Li Chong's meaning is that according to the law text, an adopted son is not implicated when his birth father commits a crime; therefore when the adoptive father commits a crime he should be implicated. Without the character "not" the text is untenable; it is now supplied accordingly.
70
不稱子不從父百衲本此句作「稱子不不從父」，顯誤，北本、汲本、殿本作「稱子不從父」，南本、局本如上摘句。 冊府 〈同上卷頁〉 作「不言子不從父」。 按百衲本「稱」上「不」字誤移在「子」字下，致不成語，北、汲、殿三本刪一「不」字，上下語意不貫，冊府「稱」字作「言」，但上同有「不」字，知南本、局本是，今從之。
"Does not say that the son does not follow the father": the Baiwan edition of this sentence reads "says son not-not follow father," which is clearly wrong; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions read "says son not follow father"; the Southern and Bureau editions read as in the excerpt above. Cefu (same juan and page) reads "does not say son not follow father." In the Baiwan edition the character "not" above "says" was wrongly moved below "son," making the phrase unintelligible; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions delete one "not," but the sense above and below does not cohere; in Cefu the character "says" is written "speak," but above it likewise has "not," so the Southern and Bureau editions are correct; the text follows them.
71
於典矯也諸本「典」訛「曲」，不可通，今據冊府 〈同上卷頁〉 改。
"Distorts the canon": all editions corrupt "canon" as "bent"; the text is untenable; restored according to Cefu (same juan and page) Corrected.
72
沖時震怒諸本「怒」作「恐」，北史卷一００自序、冊府卷四七八 〈五七一０頁〉 作「怒」。 按下文極言李沖暴怒之狀，且李彪與沖權勢不敵，沖何故震恐？ 「恐」乃「怒」之形訛，今據改。
"Chong was then furious": all editions read "furious" as "fearful"; Beishi, juan 100, author's preface, and Cefu, juan 478 (p. 5710) have "furious." The text below strongly describes Li Chong's violent rage, and Li Biao's power did not match Chong's — why should Chong have been stricken with fear? "Fearful" is a graphic corruption of "furious"; the text is emended accordingly.
